text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty PDR-78912 fired -> High 5xx rate on router-eu-prod (alert: router.errors.percent > 5% over 1m). Auto-escalation to eng-oncall. link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PDR-78912

Lisa (oncall): acked — I'm on it, looking at router-eu-prod metrics now :eyes:

incident-bot: Alert details:
- metric: router.errors.percent
- current: 6.8%
- threshold: 5% (1m)
- affected nodes: router-eu-prod-0..3
- recent events: spike at 6133334430

Miguel: I see a sharp spike in inbound connections at the same time on the service load balancer — looks like a canary job exec. Could be a synthetic-canary run flooding the pool.

Ryan: pulling logs, running a quick grep on router errors:
```
kubectl -n prod logs router-eu-prod-0 | tail -n 200 | grep "upstream timeout"
# sample:
# 2026-07-12T10:07:10Z WARN upstream timeout id=abcd duration=1200ms
```

Sara: autoscaler triggered a scale-out ~2m ago, added 2 routers, but the error rate stayed high for a bit while connection pools warmed up. Might be transient.

Kevin: any recent deploys? I don't see a normal deploy in the window — only the automated synthetic-canary job that hits healthchecks. Ops-bot shows job run id: sc-20260712-1123.

Anya: Can we check synthetic-canary logs? If it misconfigured and hammered /generate paths we could overload router connection pools.

Lisa (oncall): pinging the canary owner, and silencing PD for 10m while we confirm (silence cmd used). :lock:

Miguel: quick grep on synthetic-runner logs:
```
ssh runner@canary-1
cat /var/log/canary/sc-20260712-1123.log | tail -n 80
# shows repeated POST /v1/generate at ~1500 rps for 30s
```

Ryan: ok, that's consistent. Connection pool exhaustion made a portion of requests fail with 502/504 during spike. After autoscale finished and canary rate dropped, error rate decayed.

Lisa (oncall): I'm going to pause the synthetic-runner and let routers stabilize. pausing job via CI: `ci pause-job sc-20260712-1123`

ops-bot: synthetic-canary sc-20260712-1123 paused by Lisa (oncall).

Sara: metrics: router.errors.percent back to 0.8% and request latency back to normal within 90s after pause. No major customer impact observed in rollout metrics.

incident-bot: PagerDuty PDR-78912 auto-resolved after 3 minutes (error rate fell below threshold).

Lisa (oncall): marking this as no-customer-impact, short-lived noisy canary. Filing follow-up with CI team to add rate limits and circuit-breaker on synthetic-canary (prevent hitting /v1/generate at high RPS). Assigning to Miguel for follow-up.

Miguel: will add token bucket limiter and a randomized ramp for the canary, and add a dashboard alert specifically for synthetic job rampups so it doesn't overlap with prod alerts.

Kevin: recommend creating a derived alert that ignores canary-tagged source IPs or job ids — avoids false positives.

Anya: I'll draft a short postmortem note: root cause = synthetic-canary misconfiguration (no client-side rate limiting) -> transient router pool exhaustion -> autoscale handled capacity -> auto-resolve. No customer-facing errors detected.

Lisa (oncall): good. I'll close out here and move a short summary to #postmortems later. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

Ryan: logging snapshot saved to s3://redwood-incident-logs/6133334444/; will attach to the postmortem.

Kevin: adding follow-up ticket in ops backlog: OPS-1248 (canary rate limits + ignore-list for prod alerts).

incident-bot: Reminder: if this reoccurs, PagerDuty escalation will continue. For now, incident closed.

Lisa (oncall): handoff to Miguel for remediation work during next business day. Leaving channel. :wave:
